figures.description: Elements of a Soil Nail Wall Design and specification of soil nail wall components. Three main components: soil nails, facing, and ancillary elements Soil nail tendons: #6 to #10 bars (19-32 mm), Grade 60 or 75 Typical spacing: 1.2-1.8 m horizontal and vertical Typical inclination: 10-20 degrees below horizontal Initial facing: 75-100 mm shotcrete with WWM Final facing: 150-200 mm CIP concrete or shotcrete Drainage: geocomposite strips and toe drain pipe

figures.description: Construction Sequence Construction sequencing for all soil nail wall projects. Top-down construction in 1-2 m lifts Drill holes, install tendons with centralizers, grout from bottom up Install drainage strips before shotcrete if needed Apply initial shotcrete facing with WWM Secure bearing plates with hex nuts Repeat for each excavation lift Install final facing after all nails are placed

figures.description: Soil Nail Wall Components Material selection and specification for soil nail wall components. Tendons: ASTM A615 Grade 60 (420 MPa) or Grade 75 (520 MPa), or ASTM A722 Grade 150 Common bar diameters: #6 to #10 (19-32 mm) Hollow (self-drilling) bars also used Bearing plates: typically 200x200x19 mm Grout: neat cement, minimum 21 MPa at 28 days, w/c = 0.40-0.50 Grout transfers loads and provides corrosion protection Headed studs connect nail to final facing

figures.description: Construction Methods Construction methodology for all soil nail wall projects. Drilling: rotary or percussion, 100-200 mm diameter holes Open-hole in stable soils; cased drilling in collapsible ground Grouting: tremie from bottom up, neat cement grout Pressure grouting may increase bond in marginal soils Initial shotcrete facing: 75-100 mm thick, dry or wet mix WWM reinforcement: W1.4 or W2.0 on 100x100 mm grid Centralizers every 2.5 m for minimum grout cover Final facing: 150-200 mm CIP concrete or shotcrete

Potential limit states in soil nail walls: (a) internal stability (slip surface intersecting soil and nails); (b) global stability (slip surface not intersecting nails); (c) global stability: basal heave; (d) geotechnical strength: lateral sliding; (e) geotechnical strength: pullout; (f) structural strength: nail in tension; (g) facing structural strength: bending; (h) facing structural strength: punching shear; (i) facing structural strength: headed stud in tension
figures.description: Limit States Complete list of limit state checks required for soil nail wall design. Overall stability: internal, global, and basal heave Geotechnical strength: lateral sliding, nail pullout Structural strength: nail tension, facing bending, punching shear, headed stud tension Extreme event: earthquake loading Service: lateral displacement and wall settlement Each limit state has specific resistance factors (Tables 5.4-5.11)

figures.description: Overall Stability of Soil Nail Walls Overall stability evaluation including internal, global, and basal heave checks. Internal stability: slip surface through nails with pullout resistance Global stability: slip surface beyond nails with no nail contribution Basal heave: soft fine-grained soils beneath excavation Limit-equilibrium programs: SNAIL, SNAILZ, GoldNail, SNAP-2 Factored resistance: phi * [(W+Q)cos(alpha) + T*sin(beta)] * tan(phi_s) (Eq 5.6) Factored driving force: gamma*(W+Q)*sin(alpha) - T*cos(beta) (Eq 5.7) Resistance factors: static phi_OS = 0.65, seismic phi_OS = 0.90 (Table 5.4)

figures.description: Geotechnical Strength Limit States Geotechnical strength limit state checks for pullout and lateral sliding. Pullout resistance factors: static phi_PO = 0.65, seismic phi_PO = 0.65 (Table 5.6) Pullout factors valid when bond verified by field load testing Lateral sliding: rigid block model with earth pressure behind wall phi_LS * R_s >= gamma_EH * Pa * cos(delta) + gamma_ES * ES (Eq 5.17) R_s = c_b * B_L + (W + Pa * sin(delta)) * tan(phi'_fb) (Eq 5.18) Pa = gamma_s * H_1^2 * Ka / 2 (Eq 5.19) Ka by Coulomb (Eq 5.21) or Rankine (Eq 5.22, 5.23) theory Lateral sliding factors: static phi_LS = 1.00, seismic phi_LS = 0.90 (Table 5.7)

figures.description: Service Limit States (Deformations) Deformation estimation and service limit state evaluation for soil nail walls. delta_v approximately equal to delta_h = (delta_h/H)_i * H (Eq 5.30) delta_h/H: 1/1000 (rock/stiff), 1/500 (sandy), 1/333 (fine-grained) (Table 5.12) Deformation zone: D_DEF = C * (1 - tan(alpha)) * H (Eq 5.31) C values: 0.8 (rock/stiff), 1.25 (sandy), 1.5 (fine-grained) Valid for L/H >= 0.7, negligible surcharge, FS_OS >= 1.5 Construction deflections > 0.005H are cause for concern Post-construction deformations may increase 15% over 6 months
